about: One card per technique the kit can do. scripts/technique.py check compares it with the code (both ways), the docs and selftest.sh; scripts/technique.py search finds a technique by name or by the names editors use. Adding one: references/adding-techniques.md.

techniques.name: Title
techniques.about: A heading in one of five styles (outline, stack, gradient, glass, marker) with one accent word and an optional sub-line. One per beat.
techniques.plan: Overlays: title | top | style=outline; lines=Line A / Line B; accent=B

techniques.name: Callout
techniques.about: A dot pops on a part of the picture, a leader line draws and a frosted label slides in from the margin. Only on a static moment.

techniques.name: Highlight
techniques.about: A hand-drawn circle, underline or arrow draws on around the subject.

techniques.name: Step chip
techniques.about: A numbered chip with one instruction, synced to the voice.

techniques.name: Checklist
techniques.about: Rows with ticks that draw on, staggered; three or four rows.
techniques.plan: checklist | upper | items=A / B / C; title=Terms

techniques.name: Price
techniques.about: A count-up price with a pulse and an optional struck-through old price; must match the listing exactly.

techniques.name: Cart arrow
techniques.about: A hand-drawn arrow curves down onto the TikTok Shop product bar's bag tile, draws on and bobs. Feed videos on TikTok Shop only.

techniques.name: Sticker badge
techniques.about: A rotated badge that pops and wobbles; one per video, never a claim.

techniques.name: Progress bar
techniques.about: A bar that fills across its life, for time passing.

techniques.name: Magnifier
techniques.about: A lens showing a 2.2x crop of a clip at a point, for fine detail; keep the camera still meanwhile.

techniques.name: Three-photo header
techniques.about: A strip of up to three framed stills across the top with a caption each, landing on the spoken words; turns a spoken list of three into something the eye can scan.
techniques.plan: thumbs | top | cards=CLIP_A@3.0:Item A+@"item a" / CLIP_B@1.5:Item B / CLIP_C@0.8:Item C

techniques.name: Before/after card
techniques.about: BEFORE and AFTER frames of the same item with labels, the AFTER arriving over a dark scrim; honest time note. Not allowed in boosted ads on TikTok.
techniques.plan: compare | top | before=CLIP_A@1.6; after=CLIP_A@27.6; mode=side; note=Shortened

techniques.name: Ranking podium
techniques.about: Glossy tiles on podiums for a listicle; no third-party logos without rights.

techniques.name: Lower third
techniques.about: A name bar with a role, two to three seconds; credentials must be real.

techniques.name: Spec list
techniques.about: Up to six facts with line icons, popping in turn; facts come from the documents.
techniques.plan: specs | upper | items=area:85 m² / bed:3 / bath:2; title=Details

techniques.name: Map pin
techniques.about: A pin drops with a ring; the place name and a second line slide in.

techniques.name: Label
techniques.about: A quiet tag (name plus detail) with a line drawing under it: rooms, dishes, items.

techniques.name: Stat
techniques.about: One figure counting up with a unit and a label; a real number with a source.

techniques.name: Bar chart
techniques.about: Two to five horizontal bars growing in turn with counting values, the largest highlighted. Real measurements only.
techniques.plan: chart | upper | items=A#45 / B#120; unit=min; highlight=B

techniques.name: Image card
techniques.about: A still from public/ scaling in, framed or bare: floor plans, logos, packshots.

techniques.name: Timeline panel with playhead
techniques.about: A screenshot of an editor's timeline (any file in public/) with a white playhead sweeping across it at constant speed over the overlay's length: the signature of a technique-breakdown video, showing where in the edit the demonstrated moment lives.
techniques.plan: timelinePanel | bottom | src=images/timeline.png; width=900; at=0.5,0.74; from=0.04; to=0.96

params.desc: the screenshot, a file under public/
centre of the panel as fractions of the frame
width of the panel
playhead x at the start, as a fraction of the panel's width
playhead x at the end
playhead colour

techniques.use_when: a tutorial or showreel that shows how each moment was built; a real screenshot of the user's own project
techniques.avoid_when: a made-up screenshot presented as the real project (never fake a timeline)
techniques.timing: the playhead moves linearly for the whole overlay; the panel fades in over 8 frames
techniques.source: measured on two technique-breakdown videos: a still screenshot of the whole edit with a playhead at a constant 15-22 px/s
techniques.test: showreel transitions: six presentations, the occluder finder and the reverse tool

techniques.name: Shout burst
techniques.about: The opening shout as a pile of tilted copies: a ghost under, then more and more copies each larger and nearer the edge.

techniques.name: Phrase
techniques.about: A white lead line over a loud emphasis line; letters scatter in and fly apart. Every spoken thought can be a block; `fx` picks the animation.
techniques.plan: phrase | top | lead=Lead; emph=LOUD; emphColor=yellow; fx=slam

techniques.name: Pill
techniques.about: A rounded label whose text types in; white or red; lists of two or three offers.

techniques.name: Arc text
techniques.about: Letters along an arc with echoes fanning out behind them; the opening shout, once.

techniques.name: Handwritten phrase
techniques.about: One handwritten phrase in the highlight colour, letters scattering in; one per video.

techniques.name: Tag
techniques.about: A small loud label popping over a card: kinds of work or clients.

techniques.name: Logo
techniques.about: The brand mark arrives out of a motion blur and snaps sharp; `hold=1` for an end card. Needs the owner's own file.

techniques.name: Range counter
techniques.about: A number pops, an arrow draws, the second number pops and a unit slides up: one spoken range.

techniques.name: Pictogram
techniques.about: A pictogram popping in at a point (target, megaphone, bang, search, check); not on faces.

techniques.name: Circled label
techniques.about: A label that a hand-drawn ellipse draws around, with a pictogram popping in below.

techniques.name: Raw vs final
techniques.about: Two cards side by side playing the same take, the unedited clip and the finished look: an honest 'what editing does'.

techniques.name: Punch-in
techniques.about: A pseudo-component: a keyword punch-in on the camera at a moment (a quick scale bump).

techniques.name: Sound cue
techniques.about: A pseudo-component: a sound effect placed at a moment (a name from the sfx bank).

techniques.name: Hard cut
techniques.about: No overlap: the next scene replaces the last on one frame; the default for beat-cut genres.

techniques.name: Cross-dissolve
techniques.about: The incoming scene fades over the outgoing one.

techniques.name: Slide / push
techniques.about: The new shot pushes the old one off in a direction.

techniques.name: Soft wipe
techniques.about: A soft-edged wipe across the frame; good for before to after.

techniques.name: Iris
techniques.about: A circle opens from the centre; a hero reveal.

techniques.name: Push cut
techniques.about: A hard cut with a scale punch and a two-frame flash: the TikTok-native accent.

techniques.name: Zoom through
techniques.about: Scale through the cut with a blur peak, as if flying through the picture.

techniques.name: Blur dissolve
techniques.about: A dissolve that passes through a blur.

techniques.name: Whip pan
techniques.about: A fast directional slide with motion blur; hides a cut in a camera whip.

techniques.name: Card flip
techniques.about: A 3D card flip; sparingly.

techniques.name: Cross zoom
techniques.about: A radial zoom blur between shots (WebGL in Remotion, a zoom-blur dissolve in HyperFrames).
techniques.source: gl-transitions CrossZoom (MIT)

techniques.name: Card slide
techniques.about: Card layout: the outgoing card slides off with a trail of copies and the next card slides in.

techniques.name: Card swirl
techniques.about: The incoming shot arrives as a stack of tilted cards that straighten into the full frame.

techniques.name: Camera shake
techniques.about: A short handheld-style shake on the cut; HyperFrames only.

techniques.name: Glitch hit
techniques.about: A digital glitch (slice shifts and colour split) on the cut; HyperFrames only.

techniques.name: RGB split
techniques.about: A real colour-channel split (SVG filter) that settles; HyperFrames only.

techniques.name: Beat pulse
techniques.about: A quick scale and brightness pulse on the cut; HyperFrames only.

techniques.name: Scatter
techniques.about: Letters fly in from random places and settle; fly apart on exit. The default loud line.

techniques.name: Drop
techniques.about: Letters fall from above and bounce.

techniques.name: Wave
techniques.about: Letters rise in a ripple and keep rippling.

techniques.name: Elastic
techniques.about: Rubbery overshoot, letter by letter.

techniques.name: Letter flip
techniques.about: Letters flip up in 3D.

techniques.name: Slam
techniques.about: The whole line slams in from 3x size and shakes: a shout or claim.

techniques.name: Stamp
techniques.about: Tilted, lands with an overshoot, a double rule pressed round it: a verdict.

techniques.name: Glitch text
techniques.about: RGB-split jitter that settles; for the problem or pain.

techniques.name: Neon
techniques.about: Flickers on then glows; a call to action.

techniques.name: Shine
techniques.about: A light sweep crosses the finished text.

techniques.name: Mask wipe
techniques.about: A coloured bar wipes the text into view.

techniques.name: Split
techniques.about: Two halves slide in from opposite sides and join.

techniques.name: Typewriter
techniques.about: Letters appear one by one with a cursor.

techniques.name: Rise
techniques.about: A quiet rise: the calm default.

techniques.name: Outline title
techniques.about: Coloured fill with a dark outline drawn under the fill; reads on any footage. The default for demos.

techniques.name: Stack title
techniques.about: A stacked heading with a gradient main line and an accent word.

techniques.name: Gradient title
techniques.about: Gradient-filled heading; avoid over white fabric.

techniques.name: Glass title
techniques.about: Frosted glass plate behind dark gradient text.

techniques.name: Marker title
techniques.about: Highlighter-marker blocks behind the words.

techniques.name: Karaoke captions
techniques.about: Whole phrase on screen with the spoken word highlighted.

techniques.name: Pop captions
techniques.about: One to three words at a time, each popping in on its own timing; talking heads, fashion.

techniques.name: Plain captions
techniques.about: The phrase only, no highlight.

techniques.name: No captions
techniques.about: No captions at all (the visuals or titles carry the words).

techniques.name: Colour highlight
techniques.about: The spoken word turns the highlight colour and swells.

techniques.name: Box highlight
techniques.about: A rounded block hugs the spoken word and hops to the next.

techniques.name: Underline highlight
techniques.about: A bar draws under the spoken word.

techniques.name: Glow highlight
techniques.about: A halo glows around the spoken word.

techniques.name: Push in
techniques.about: A slow visible scale-in toward the focus point.

techniques.name: Pull out
techniques.about: A scale-out that reveals more of the scene.

techniques.name: Pan
techniques.about: A sideways drift across the frame at a fixed scale.

techniques.name: Hold
techniques.about: A near-static frame with a tiny scale so the picture is not dead.

techniques.name: Keyframed camera
techniques.about: Two to four named framings (zoom, point, roll) with an easing per segment, like CapCut keyframes; the frame edge never shows.

techniques.name: Linear
techniques.about: Constant rate: mechanical, for loops.

techniques.name: Ease in
techniques.about: Starts slow, ends fast.

techniques.name: Ease out
techniques.about: Starts fast, settles: the natural arrival.

techniques.name: Ease in-out
techniques.about: Slow both ends.

techniques.name: Soft
techniques.about: A gentle in-out with a long tail for premium moves.

techniques.name: Snap
techniques.about: Very fast start, hard stop: a punch.

techniques.name: Back
techniques.about: Overshoots by about 8% then settles; once per video.

techniques.name: Hold segment
techniques.about: The value stays until the next key, then jumps.

techniques.name: No grade
techniques.about: No look: corrections only.

techniques.name: Natural
techniques.about: True to life with a little punch: demos, tutorials, talking heads.

techniques.name: Bright interior
techniques.about: Lifted shadows and mids, clean whites, slightly warm; colours kept honest.

techniques.name: Warm food
techniques.about: Warm, a little more contrast and saturation, highlights kept.

techniques.name: Soft skin
techniques.about: Gentle contrast, warm skin, protected highlights; fabric colours not pushed.

techniques.name: Vivid
techniques.about: Rich colour and a firm S-curve, not neon: montages and promos.

techniques.name: Cool theme
techniques.about: White and sky blue: demos, tutorials, talking heads, promos.

techniques.name: Warm theme
techniques.about: Ivory, gold, vermilion, brown: food and amber-lit footage.

techniques.name: Luxe theme
techniques.about: Ivory, champagne gold, charcoal: property, fashion, beauty.

techniques.name: Crimson theme
techniques.about: White, strong red, yellow highlight, deep maroon: a bold high-energy look with a maroon animated grid behind cards.

techniques.name: Silhouette fill / flash
techniques.about: The subject filled with a colour; blinking on a few frames it is the silhouette flash opener before the video plays.

techniques.name: Subject outline
techniques.about: A ring of a few pixels around the subject (never over it), for one emphasised beat.

techniques.name: Subject glow
techniques.about: A soft coloured halo around the subject.

techniques.name: Spotlight (dim)
techniques.about: Everything except the subject is darkened, a spotlight on the person or product.

techniques.name: Colour pop
techniques.about: Everything except the subject turns grey; the subject keeps its colour.

techniques.name: Text behind subject
techniques.about: Big text between the footage and a cut-out copy of the subject, so the person stands in front of the words. Needs a clean matte on every frame.
techniques.plan: Subject: behind 0-80 @ mattes/CLIP_A; every=2; text=WORD; size=320

techniques.name: Film burn
techniques.about: A warm overexposed burn washes through the cut, like a strip of film catching light; food, fashion, nostalgia. Two per video at most, never on a reveal.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Zoom blur
techniques.about: A zoom-blur between the shots, hiding the cut in a rush toward the centre.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Dreamy zoom
techniques.about: A soft glowing zoom with a gentle rotation; beauty, travel, wedding.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Linear blur
techniques.about: A directional blur dissolve: the picture smears along a line while it changes.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Cross warp
techniques.about: The two shots warp into each other along a moving edge.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Zoom in-out
techniques.about: Zoom out of the old shot while zooming in to the new one: a push through a tunnel.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Blur slide
techniques.about: A slide with built-in motion blur; softer than a whip, more modern than a plain slide.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Clock wipe
techniques.about: A clock hand sweeps round and reveals the new shot.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions clock-wipe

techniques.name: Ripple
techniques.about: A water ripple spreads from the centre and carries the new shot in.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Burn dissolve
techniques.about: A glowing burning edge eats the old shot away to reveal the new one.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions dissolve (named burnDissolve here to keep 'dissolve' for the cross-dissolve)

techniques.name: Cube
techniques.about: The two shots are faces of a 3D cube that rotates.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions cube

techniques.name: Book flip
techniques.about: A page turn: the old shot folds away like a page.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Swap
techniques.about: The two shots swap places in depth, one passing in front of the other with a reflection.
techniques.source: Remotion @remotion/transitions (shader, HTML-in-canvas; MIT-style gl-transitions heritage); software GL: SVK_GL=swangle (default)

techniques.name: Blinds
techniques.about: Horizontal blinds open onto the new shot and meet: a clean, graphic wipe.
techniques.source: written for the kit (CSS mask)

techniques.name: Diamond reveal
techniques.about: A diamond opens from the centre of the frame onto the new shot.
techniques.source: written for the kit (CSS clip-path)

techniques.name: Doors
techniques.about: The old shot splits down the middle and the halves slide apart, uncovering the new shot. HyperFrames shows the new shot through a widening slit instead (halves do not move).
techniques.source: written for the kit (CSS clip-path)

techniques.name: Glitch slice
techniques.about: Through the cut the picture is sliced into bands that jump sideways with a hue split; old shot first half, new shot second half. HyperFrames approximates it with one jitter and a hue split.
techniques.source: written for the kit (CSS clip-path bands)

techniques.name: Spin zoom
techniques.about: The old shot spins and grows into a blur; the new one spins in from the other side and settles.
techniques.source: written for the kit (CSS transform + blur)

techniques.name: Teal and orange
techniques.about: Cinematic split tone, skin-safe: teal shadows, orange highlights, mids untouched. Not for white garments or close-up skin; soften with --grade-strength.
techniques.source: ffmpeg colorbalance (docs); numbers are the kit's own, tested for direction in selftest.sh
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Cinematic fade
techniques.about: Lifted blacks and slightly muted colour: the matte filmic look.
techniques.source: ffmpeg colorlevels (docs); numbers are the kit's own
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Moody
techniques.about: Darker, cooler and contrasty: night, tech, drama; check caption contrast on a phone.
techniques.source: ffmpeg curves/colorbalance; numbers are the kit's own
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Pastel / airy
techniques.about: Soft, light and airy: lifted shadows, gentle colour. White text vanishes on it.
techniques.source: ffmpeg curves/eq; numbers are the kit's own
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Vintage film
techniques.about: Faded film: tinted lifted blacks, muted colour; add grain and vignette with look.grain / look.vignette.
techniques.source: ffmpeg curves (docs); numbers are the kit's own
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Black and white
techniques.about: High-contrast black and white with Rec.709 luma weights and an S-curve.
techniques.source: Rec.709 luma coefficients
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Bleach bypass
techniques.about: Desaturated, hard and gritty. Never for fashion, food or beauty demos.
techniques.source: bleach-bypass description (premiumbeat.com tutorial); numbers are the kit's own
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Golden hour
techniques.about: Warm low-sun look: a 4500 K push (lower kelvin is warmer), orange highlights.
techniques.source: ffmpeg colortemperature (direction measured here); numbers are the kit's own
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Cold blue
techniques.about: Cool blue (8500 K), slightly desaturated: tech, winter, clinical; keep strength low on people.
techniques.source: ffmpeg colortemperature; numbers are the kit's own
techniques.test: grades move a synthetic card

techniques.name: Roll
techniques.about: A slow tilt of the frame (degrees from scene start to end) that makes a static shot lean like a handheld one.

techniques.name: Focus point
techniques.about: The point of the footage that stays put while the camera scales: the product, a face.

techniques.name: Pan distance
techniques.about: How far a pan travels, as a fraction of the frame width.

techniques.name: Handheld shake
techniques.about: Procedural handheld sway on top of any move (smooth noise on x, y and roll, each axis with its own seed); the frame is scaled to hide the edge. mild = 6 px, strong = 14 px.
techniques.source: smooth value-noise sway (octaves 0.9/2.3/5.1 Hz); recipe from the HyperFrames camera-shake block's design notes, re-derived without its constants
techniques.test: camera shake parses

techniques.name: Speed ramp
techniques.about: A custom curve: speeds at evenly spaced points across the scene, eased between (ramp 1>2.5>1).

techniques.name: Montage curve
techniques.about: Slow-fast-slow: a push through the middle of the scene.
techniques.source: CapCut velocity preset names; the numbers are the kit's own approximations
techniques.test: speed presets parse

techniques.name: Hero curve
techniques.about: Fast-slow-fast: a slow moment held in the middle; needs a 60 fps proxy.
techniques.source: CapCut velocity preset names; the numbers are the kit's own approximations
techniques.test: speed presets parse

techniques.name: Bullet time curve
techniques.about: A sudden near-freeze then release; needs a 60 fps proxy.
techniques.source: CapCut velocity preset names; the numbers are the kit's own approximations
techniques.test: speed presets parse

techniques.name: Flash in
techniques.about: Starts fast and settles to normal speed.
techniques.source: CapCut velocity preset names; the numbers are the kit's own approximations
techniques.test: speed presets parse

techniques.name: Flash out
techniques.about: Runs at normal speed then whips away fast.
techniques.source: CapCut velocity preset names; the numbers are the kit's own approximations
techniques.test: speed presets parse

techniques.name: Saturation push
techniques.about: A global saturation factor on the footage only (1 = unchanged); the cheap lift of a flat 1080p clip.

techniques.name: Contrast push
techniques.about: A global contrast factor on the footage only.

techniques.name: Brightness push
techniques.about: A global brightness factor on the footage only.

techniques.name: Warm tint
techniques.about: A sepia-style warm tint on the footage (0.06 = a little).

techniques.name: Vignette
techniques.about: A darkened edge (0..1, subtle 0.2-0.4) over the whole picture, under the graphics.
techniques.test: look fx parses

techniques.name: Film grain
techniques.about: Fine noise over the picture that changes every sixth frame (0..1, subtle 0.04-0.1).
techniques.test: look fx parses

techniques.name: Scramble
techniques.about: Random glyphs flicker, then lock into the real letters left to right (about 0.8 s). 1-3 words; hold it after the lock; never on spoken captions.
techniques.plan: phrase | top | emph=RESULTS ARE IN; fx=scramble
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: Blur-in
techniques.about: Each word sharpens out of a soft blur while shrinking from 112%, word after word. A gentle, dreamy opening line.
techniques.plan: phrase | top | emph=Light as a cloud; fx=blurin
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: Tracking-in
techniques.about: Wide letter-spacing closes to none while the line fades in. For a short brand or title line (about 14 characters at most).
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: Slice reveal
techniques.about: Three bands of the line slide in from alternating sides and snap together; the top band stays whole so Vietnamese marks are not cut.
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: Word pop
techniques.about: Each word springs in tilted from 60% and settles, one after another, so the line bounces along with the voice.
techniques.plan: phrase | top | emph=Light as a cloud sweet as a dream; fx=popword
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: Split-flap
techniques.about: Airport-board cells flip through glyphs and land on the real ones. For digits and capitals: a price, a countdown, a short offer.
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: Strike and replace
techniques.about: `OLD -> NEW`: a red bar strikes the old text out and dims it, the new text springs in beside it. Only real earlier values.
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: Underline draw
techniques.about: The line stays still while a hand-drawn wavy underline wipes in beneath it. Put it on the lowest line of a block.
techniques.plan: phrase | top | emph=Light as a cloud; fx=draw
techniques.source: assets/remotion-template/src/components/text/Fx.tsx

techniques.name: League Spartan

techniques.name: Ink bleed
techniques.about: Ink drops grow from a few points, swell and merge into the new shot: SVG circles blurred and thresholded (goo), the edge torn by a noise displacement, a final fill so the end is the full frame. Both renderers draw the same SVG mask.
techniques.source: written for the kit (SVG goo mask: feGaussianBlur + alpha threshold + feTurbulence displacement)

techniques.name: Luma wipe
techniques.about: A luma mask (a gradient from the side the new shot comes from, broken up by noise) is thresholded at a level that rises with the progress, so the dark parts of the mask show the new shot first and the edge is ragged and soft. Direction parameter. Both renderers.
techniques.source: written for the kit (generated SVG feTurbulence mask, no texture file)

techniques.name: Cut the curve
techniques.about: A hard cut hidden in a move: the old shot accelerates along the axis, the picture is swapped at peak speed, the new shot carries the same move on and settles. No blur; both shots are scaled up while off centre so no edge shows. Direction parameter; match it to the camera move.
techniques.source: written for the kit (CSS translate and scale, mirrored accelerating curves)

techniques.name: GL pixelate
techniques.about: Both shots break into square blocks that grow to a peak in the middle and shrink away again; the swap happens at the peak. GL shader, Remotion only.
techniques.source: kit-original GLSL in the gl-transitions convention (shaders/pixelate.glsl, loaded by engine/glTransitions.tsx); Remotion only, HyperFrames draws a fade

techniques.name: GL directional warp
techniques.about: A soft wipe whose edge waves, stretching the old shot along the edge while the new shot settles in behind it. Direction parameter. GL shader, Remotion only.
techniques.source: kit-original GLSL in the gl-transitions convention (shaders/directionalWarp.glsl, loaded by engine/glTransitions.tsx); Remotion only, HyperFrames draws a fade

techniques.name: GL swirl
techniques.about: The picture twists around the centre, strongest in the middle of the move, and the new shot untwists out of it. GL shader, Remotion only.
techniques.source: kit-original GLSL in the gl-transitions convention (shaders/swirl.glsl, loaded by engine/glTransitions.tsx); Remotion only, HyperFrames draws a fade

techniques.name: GL mosaic
techniques.about: The frame is a grid; a square opens from the middle of every cell and grows until the new shot fills it, cells starting in a diagonal order from the side the new shot comes from. Direction parameter. GL shader, Remotion only.
techniques.source: kit-original GLSL in the gl-transitions convention (shaders/mosaic.glsl, loaded by engine/glTransitions.tsx); Remotion only, HyperFrames draws a fade

techniques.name: GL RGB split
techniques.about: A dissolve in which the red, green and blue channels cross-fade at different times and slide apart sideways, so the colours fringe and snap back together. Direction parameter. GL shader, Remotion only.
techniques.source: kit-original GLSL in the gl-transitions convention (shaders/rgbSplit.glsl, loaded by engine/glTransitions.tsx); Remotion only, HyperFrames draws a fade

techniques.name: GL radial shutter
techniques.about: The new shot opens through a fan of blades around the centre, like the shutter of a camera lens; a twist parameter bends the blades into a spiral. GL shader, Remotion only.
techniques.source: kit-original GLSL in the gl-transitions convention (shaders/radialShutter.glsl, loaded by engine/glTransitions.tsx); Remotion only, HyperFrames draws a fade

techniques.name: GL ripple pixel
techniques.about: A ring spreads from the centre; inside it the new shot, outside the old one, and along the ring the picture is pixelated and pushed outward in a wave. GL shader, Remotion only.
techniques.source: kit-original GLSL in the gl-transitions convention (shaders/ripplePixel.glsl, loaded by engine/glTransitions.tsx); Remotion only, HyperFrames draws a fade

techniques.name: Grid flash reveal
techniques.about: A 3 x 3 grid over the old shot: in a random order each cell goes flat cream for one frame and is then the new shot, thin dark lines stay between the cells, and two cream frames close it. Cream, never pure white. About 0.6 s.
techniques.test: showreel transitions: six presentations, the occluder finder and the reverse tool
techniques.use_when: between two shots of different content on a beat; a tech, product or showreel video
techniques.avoid_when: a calm or emotional shot, or more than once every few seconds
techniques.timing: 18 frames; cells open from 4 % to 78 % of the transition, 9 % of it cream per cell, lines from 12 % to 88 %, a closing cream flash from 88 % to 96 %
techniques.source: measured on two public technique-breakdown videos (references/transition-pack.md), drawn with CSS and SVG masks
techniques.renderer_notes: HyperFrames draws a fade (project_to_hyperframes.py lists it under Remotion only).

techniques.name: Frame click (crop pop)
techniques.about: The new shot, scaled down, pops open as a window low in the middle of the frame over the old shot and grows to the full frame with an ease-out in about 8 frames: a camera-click cut.
techniques.test: showreel transitions: six presentations, the occluder finder and the reverse tool
techniques.use_when: a run of cuts on the beat about a second apart; the new shot must read at a third of its size
techniques.avoid_when: a new shot whose subject is tiny or only readable full size
techniques.timing: 8 frames, ease-out cubic; the window starts 46 % of the frame wide at x 27 %, y 52 %
techniques.source: measured on two public technique-breakdown videos (references/transition-pack.md), drawn with CSS and SVG masks
techniques.renderer_notes: HyperFrames draws a fade (project_to_hyperframes.py lists it under Remotion only).

techniques.name: Crop with negative
techniques.about: The same window pop, a smaller window at the lower right of centre, shown as an inverted black-and-white picture for its first half and turning to colour as it fills the frame.
techniques.test: showreel transitions: six presentations, the occluder finder and the reverse tool
techniques.use_when: one accent per video on a punch beat; a high-contrast new shot
techniques.avoid_when: skin-tone heavy shots (the negative looks sick), or twice in a row
techniques.timing: 8 frames; the window starts 22 % wide at x 56 %, y 50 %; inverted for the first 50 % of the progress, back to colour by 80 %
techniques.source: measured on two public technique-breakdown videos (references/transition-pack.md), drawn with CSS and SVG masks
techniques.renderer_notes: HyperFrames draws a fade (project_to_hyperframes.py lists it under Remotion only).

techniques.name: Flash wipe (teleport band)
techniques.about: A cream band wider than the frame sweeps across in about 12 frames (fast in the middle) with soft edges; the picture is swapped while it covers everything. Used for the teleport: the same locked-off place, the subject somewhere else.
techniques.test: showreel transitions: six presentations, the occluder finder and the reverse tool
techniques.use_when: two takes from one tripod position with the subject moved; or any cut that needs a bright accent
techniques.avoid_when: handheld pairs (the background will not match under the band)
techniques.timing: 12 frames; the band is 140 % of the frame wide; left = it travels right to left; a cream wash peaks at the swap in the middle
techniques.source: measured on two public technique-breakdown videos (references/transition-pack.md), drawn with CSS and SVG masks
techniques.renderer_notes: HyperFrames draws a fade (project_to_hyperframes.py lists it under Remotion only).

techniques.name: Black flash and mix
techniques.about: Over about 14 frames the picture flickers to black and back five or so times (the frames beside a black one are dimmed: the mix) while the shot changes; the first and last frames stay clean.
techniques.test: showreel transitions: six presentations, the occluder finder and the reverse tool
techniques.use_when: night, concert, event and tech footage with a drop in the music; pair with a camera-flash sound
techniques.avoid_when: photosensitive viewers: a strobe of this kind is risky; keep it under three flashes in a second for any wide release
techniques.timing: 14 frames, one step per frame (set frames to 14 so the pattern is one per frame); black on frames 2, 3, 6, 9 and 10, the frames beside them dimmed; the new shot from frame 8
techniques.source: measured on two public technique-breakdown videos (references/transition-pack.md), drawn with CSS and SVG masks
techniques.renderer_notes: HyperFrames draws a fade (project_to_hyperframes.py lists it under Remotion only).

techniques.name: Zoom fade in
techniques.about: The old shot darkens and grows a little; the new shot fades up from black while it grows from 90 % to the full frame, a dark border showing for a few frames; a slow push can continue.
techniques.test: showreel transitions: six presentations, the occluder finder and the reverse tool
techniques.use_when: the last transition of a sequence, or a mood change; follow with a push 1.0 to 1.12
techniques.timing: 16 frames; the old shot fades out over the first half; the new one fades in from 40 % to 90 % of the progress, scale 0.9 to 1.0
techniques.source: measured on two public technique-breakdown videos (references/transition-pack.md), drawn with CSS and SVG masks
techniques.renderer_notes: HyperFrames draws a fade (project_to_hyperframes.py lists it under Remotion only).

techniques.name: Light sweep
techniques.about: A diagonal band of light crosses once in 0.6-0.8 s. Without text it lightens a feathered box; with text it draws the words and the band shines only on the letters.
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: a title, a price or a product box that earns one flash of attention
techniques.avoid_when: on every beat: repeated light reads as a template

techniques.name: Lens flare
techniques.about: A white-hot disc with a soft halo rises in 5 frames and decays, with ghosts along the line through the frame centre. One white frame at the peak with flash=1.
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: a bright source that is really in the picture (window, lamp, sun), once per video
techniques.avoid_when: on a face, or without a visible light source

techniques.name: Anamorphic streak
techniques.about: The horizontal blue line of an anamorphic lens: a white core in a coloured halo that grows from the centre in 7 frames and fades over the last 10.
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: a bright light in the shot, about 0.8 s, once per video
techniques.avoid_when: a scene with no point light

techniques.name: Knockout text
techniques.about: A colour plate over the frame with the words cut out, so the footage keeps playing inside the letters. With zoom the letters grow until their hole fills the frame, a reveal of the next shot.
techniques.plan: knockout | center | text=NEW / DROP; zoom=30; through=0.5,0.5
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: a heavy short word (12 letters per line at most) that opens or closes a video
techniques.avoid_when: busy footage under thin letters: add stroke or a darker plate

techniques.name: Text box
techniques.about: Text placed in a box you give (x, y, width, optional height as fractions of the frame), measured with the real font, wrapped at word boundaries and shrunk until it fits: it never leaves the box sideways. Colour, outline, background, alignment and any text effect are plan keys. The component a reference video's text slots are written as.
techniques.plan: textbox | – | text=Line A / Line B; box=0.1,0.4,0.8,0.12; size=72; color=#FFD21A; in=blurin
techniques.test: textbox: measured fit
techniques.use_when: the position and size of the text are known (a reference video's box, a design) and the words may be longer or shorter than the original
techniques.avoid_when: a heading in the top strip (use title) or a loud shouted line (use phrase): they have looks a plain box does not

techniques.name: Object drop
techniques.about: An object cut out of the NEXT shot falls in from the top edge (accelerating, smeared, leaning, growing a little), and on the frame it touches down the picture cuts to that shot, where the real object stands on the same spot, with a ground burst over the cut. Each landmark of a road trip, each person, room or product of a montage arrives as a landing. Pair it with `+jolt` on the scene it lands into.
techniques.plan: objectDrop | top | src=objects/OBJ_A.png; at=0.5,0.66; width=412; aspect=0.74; fall=4   (start = cut time - fall/fps; scripts/object_cutout.py prints the cell; Transition of the next scene: cut +jolt)
techniques.test: object drop: cutout script and overlays
techniques.use_when: a montage or road trip where each shot has one clear object standing on the ground (a gate, a house, a vehicle, a product on a table), at most one landing per second and five or six per video
techniques.avoid_when: on a person's face, on a shot whose object touches the frame edge (the cutout would be cut), or when the object moves across the cut

params.desc: transparent PNG under public/ (object_cutout.py writes it)
the object's bottom-centre as fractions of the frame: where it lands
the object's width as it lands
height / width of the PNG
frames of falling; the cut is on the frame after
lean at the start that straightens while falling
size on the first frame as a fraction of the landed size
how far to the side of the landing spot it starts
fraction of the object already inside the frame on the first frame
ground shadow that darkens as the object nears
frames of burst after touchdown (0 = none)
burst centre as a fraction of the frame height (default: the landing y); lift it when the ground is below the frame
radius of the spark spread (default: half the object's width, 240-400)

techniques.timing: 4 frames of fall (t squared) at 30 fps, the cut on the touchdown frame, 18 frames of burst
techniques.renderer_notes: HyperFrames does not draw it (no cutout, burst or jolt in kit.js).
techniques.source: measured on a public short video: object enters from the top edge 4 frames before touchdown, hard cut to the next shot on touchdown, 4-6 frames of flash then dust (30 fps); the burst and fall are drawn from geometry, no sample footage or sprite is used

techniques.name: Impact burst
techniques.about: The touchdown burst, layered the way a compositor stacks a ground hit: a one-frame exposure pop, a small white-hot core, spark STREAKS that fly out fast and drag to a stop, embers that fall back under gravity, dust that spreads along the ground with ragged noisy edges and thins out, a contact shadow and a faint flat shockwave ring. Squashed flat so it lies on the ground. Drawn from SVG shapes seeded by `seed`: no sprite, no stock clip.
techniques.plan: impact | top | at=0.5,0.62; size=230; flat=0.32; seed=7
techniques.test: object drop: cutout script and overlays
techniques.use_when: the beat where something lands or is set down hard (a product on a table, a door, a stamp), once per beat
techniques.avoid_when: over a face, more than one burst on screen at a time, or as a round soft glow: it must lie flat on the ground

params.desc: the ground point of the burst, fractions of the frame
radius of the spark spread
colour of the sparks' glow
colour of the dust
spark streaks (embers are a third of that again)
vertical squash (1 = a ball, lower = lying on the ground)
opacity of the flat shockwave ring (0 = none)
opacity of the one-frame exposure pop (0 = none)
changes the streaks, embers and dust puffs

techniques.timing: core 0-3 frames, streaks 3-6, embers 9-16, dust 2-17, ring 0-8, exposure pop on the first frame (30 fps)
techniques.source: measured on a public short video (4-6 frames of flash then 2 of dust); drawn from geometry

techniques.name: Echo trail
techniques.about: The same clip is drawn again a few frames behind the live frame, each copy fainter, inside the camera framing. +echo gives 2 copies, 3 frames apart, for the first 15 frames of the scene.
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: a fast move or a whip that should leave a trail
techniques.avoid_when: a calm shot: the copies just look like a stutter

techniques.name: Landing jolt
techniques.about: On the cut the whole picture is smeared sideways by a horizontal blur and shaken, both decaying to nothing over about 7 frames: the hit of something landing.
techniques.test: object drop: cutout script and overlays
techniques.use_when: the scene an objectDrop or impact lands into, once per beat
techniques.avoid_when: a calm shot, or on every cut of a video: it stops reading as a hit
techniques.timing: 7 frames, amplitude falling with the square of the time left; 36 px of blur and 26 px of shake at the cut
techniques.source: measured on a public short video: the landing frames are smeared horizontally across the whole picture for about two frames

techniques.name: Rack focus (subject)
techniques.about: The background (everything outside the person matte) goes from one blur radius to another over the window while the subject stays sharp. One video decode, no second copy.
techniques.plan: Subject: blur 0-60 @ mattes/CLIP_A; every=3; from=0; width=24
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: a reveal that should pull the eye onto the person
techniques.avoid_when: footage with no clean matte: a bad edge shows

techniques.name: Depth pop (subject)
techniques.about: A cut-out copy of the subject grows a few percent above the unchanged picture with a soft shadow that fades in, a 3D pop-out look.
techniques.plan: Subject: lift 0-45 @ mattes/CLIP_A; every=3; width=5; y=0.8; opacity=0.4
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: a freeze-hit beat over a person
techniques.avoid_when: a striped or very busy background, where only the shadow reads

techniques.name: Freeze hit
techniques.about: A scene of 0.8-1.6 s runs, holds ONE frame for its middle third and runs again, easing in and out. Dress it on the same beat with +flash and a camera punch.
techniques.test: light, subject and speed techniques compile
techniques.use_when: an impact or a pose that should land
